availability.note: Chery AU Tiggo 8 Super Hybrid page lists two grades, Urban and Ultimate, each with postcode-gated drive-away pricing and VIC 3000 novated lease figures; no Build & Price configurator on the Chery AU site. CarsGuide and CarExpert both list the same two grades for 2026/2027

listPrice.note: CarExpert 2026 Urban page: 'prices starting at $42,990' before on-road costs; CarsGuide price page lists the same MSRP (Glass's, excludes stamp duty and government charges). Chery publishes only drive-away: national $45,990 drive-away (Chery release 13 Jun 2025, still CarExpert's Sydney drive-away); Chery footnote says its drive-away includes RRP, 12 months rego, CTP, dealer delivery and stamp duty. MSRP = national DAP - $3,000 on both grades (not the -$2,000 seen on Jaecoo). Round-trip: 42,990 through calc/onroad.js gives Vic $45,675.58, $314 below the national DAP, consistent with Chery's DAP carrying dealer delivery. Plain back-out ((45990-880)/1.042 = 43,292) rejected because it absorbs dealer delivery (sources.md rule 4). Chery's VIC postcode figure could not be read (dynamic-pricing API fetch refused). $3,000 cashback 1 Nov-21 Dec 2026 is a campaign and ignored

batteryKwh.note: Chery AU spec sheet 'Battery Capacity (kWh) 18.4' LFP; Chery UK also 18.4. CarExpert variant pages and Chery's 2025 release give 18.3 (CarExpert labels it usable). Gross vs usable not settled; difference 0.5%

rangeKm.note: Chery UK Tiggo 8 Super Hybrid spec table: 56 miles WLTP = 90 km; UK car on 19in alloys, 18.4 kWh, same as AU (235/50 R19). AU spec sheet 95 km is NEDC (ADR 81/02) and higher than WLTP: rejected by direction test. Chery AU body copy also says 'up to 90km'

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: batteryKwh / rangeKm x 100 = 18.4 / 90 x 100 = 20.44. CarExpert 15.4 kWh/100km is the NEDC/weighted label figure, not used

combinedRangeKm.note: WLTP EV 90 km + 60 L tank (AU spec sheet 'Fuel Tank Capacity (L) 60') / 5.6 L/100km x 100 = 90 + 1071.4 = 1161. Chery's 1,200 km claim is NEDC-based, not used

fuelConsumptionL100km.note: Chasing Cars Urban review: 'a still very impressive 5.6L/100km' once the battery was flat (real-world review figure; no published charge-sustaining figure found: Chery UK and AU give only weighted figures). CarsGuide long-term Ultimate 6.1 then 6.9 L/100km at the pump, CarExpert ~5.8 on test, both with partial charging. Held 6.0 (attributed to an unverified 47.1 mpg UK depleted figure) replaced. Sits between siblings tiggo-7-phev 5.5 and tiggo-9-phev-elite 6.0 by mass

isFuelEfficientForLct.note: Chery AU spec sheet 'Fuel Consumption - Combined (L/100km) 1.3' (label), <= 3.5

isGreenForVicDuty.note: SRO green passenger car: combined tailpipe CO2 <= 120 g/km; CarExpert Urban page lists CO2 31 g/km combined

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: Chery UK: 117 litres 'even when all seven seats are in use'; CarExpert variant page 117 L 'to lower window' (belt line, matches convention). Chery AU spec sheet gives no boot figures

bootLitresSeatsDown.note: Chery UK: 'up to 1,930 litres' with the seats down; method not stated and likely to the roof, so reads high against the cargo-cover convention. CarExpert's 739 L 'rear seats down (VDA)' is ambiguous (probably third row only) and conflicts with 479-494 L third-row-folded figures elsewhere

towKg.note: AU spec sheet lists only 'Maximum Towing Mass (Non-Braked Trailer) 750'; no braked rating (CarExpert also 750 kg unbraked only)

warrantyYears.note: 7 years / unlimited km; condition is servicing per manufacturer guidelines and intervals, not dealer-only servicing. HV battery 8 years / unlimited (Chery AU model page)

insuranceAnnual.note: held value kept; anchored between chery-tiggo-7-phev-ultimate ($41,990, $1,550) and chery-tiggo-9-phev-elite ($52,990, $1,800)

depreciationCurve.note: Chery-group brand convention (chery-tiggo-7-phev, chery-tiggo-9-phev, chery-e5, jaecoo-j8-shs); evidence: $3,000 cashback (Nov-Dec 2026) and rolling finance/servicing campaigns on a car launched mid-2025, young brand with unproven resale
